Orbital period is 0.1769061911(28) d from the adopted spectroscopic ephemeris, converted to hours; no WD spin/beat period is inferred. Ridder+23 X-ray values are approximate 4XMM catalog band conversions, not source-specific spectral-fit fluxes; absorption convention is unspecified and radio/X-ray observations are non-simultaneous. See rawdog_measurements.csv and UGem review items for alternate distances, mass/radius branches, donor-template differences, and radio-timescale discrepancy. Echevarria+07 low-state Hα modeling estimates the disc outer edge at Rout/a≈0.61, close to the model primary Roche-lobe distance L1/a≈0.63; this is state- and Keplerian-disc-model dependent.

issues.competing_evidence: Echevarria+07 adopts optical H-alpha wing K1=107±2 km/s and K2=310±5 with i=69.7±0.7, giving M1=1.20±0.05 Msun. Long & Gilliland+99 abstract reports GHRS photospheric K1=107.1±2.1 and M1=1.12 Msun for i=67°, K2=294.7. Naylor+05 gives M1=0.91±0.01/sin^3(i), or 1.02–1.32 Msun for i=62–74°, but omits K2 systematics. Unda-Sanzana+06 optical spectra produce K1 estimates 80–~150 and cannot recover 107; they identify bright-spot asymmetry at high velocities.
issues.why_it_matters: WD mass and q inform population comparisons, but the H-alpha tracer and uncertainty assumptions are disputed; choosing one value silently would overstate precision.
issues.needed_action: For community display, decide whether to expose all conditional branches without a canonical M1, or choose a provisional solution and document which velocity/inclination evidence is prioritized. Obtain Long & Gilliland full scanned article if its detailed model assumptions are needed.

issues.competing_evidence: Naylor+05 FUV/parallax photometric radius is 5.7±0.4×10^8 cm; Long+06 FUSE uniform-WD Obs.1 model gives 5.0±0.2×10^8 cm at log g=8.5 (4.8–5.3×10^8 across log g=9–8) and 3.4×10^8 at log g=8.5 in Obs.2. Naylor+05 gravitational-redshift/inclination branch gives 4.13±0.44×10^8 cm at the lowest i and remains inconsistent by about 2.5σ. WD Teff also changes with outburst state and assumed gravity; 60–70 kK belt is non-unique.
issues.why_it_matters: A single radius or temperature could mix different epochs and model branches and misrepresent WD structure/cooling.
issues.needed_action: Keep state-specific model outputs and radius methods separate; if the wide table needs one scalar, decide whether to leave it blank or identify an explicitly provisional branch.

issues.competing_evidence: Echevarria+07 TiO template fit is M6 V (~5% light in fitted region). Naylor+05 best spectroscopic templates are M4–M5 but mass/radius/luminosity/photometric temperature compare to M2; high metallicity is proposed as an explanation, not measured. Long & Gilliland+99 calls donor M4 in abstract.
issues.why_it_matters: Donor subtype/evolution comparisons can be biased if a template fit or mass-sequence inference is treated as an intrinsic measured type.
issues.needed_action: For catalog display, decide whether to show the competing spectral diagnostics in separate fields and leave intrinsic donor Teff/type unselected; no numeric Teff was found in the checked papers.

issues.competing_evidence: Gaia DR3 parallax is 10.704757±0.033765 mas and Bailer-Jones geometric posterior is 93.057 pc [92.720,93.367], but RUWE=2.406, astrometric excess noise=0.229934 mas with significance=45.58, and Gaia marks photometry variable. HST/FGS original 1999 parallax is 10.37±0.50 mas (96.4±4.6 pc); Harrison & Johnson+04 Table 3 gives a later 9.96±0.37 mas, corresponding to 100.4±3.7 pc as cited by Long+06. The differences are modest but Gaia formal precision should not be read without quality context.
issues.why_it_matters: Distance affects unresolved M_G, radio/X-ray luminosities, and UV WD-radius normalization; RUWE/excess-noise may make formal posterior precision optimistic.
issues.needed_action: Decide whether Bailer-Jones geometric posterior remains the compatibility distance with a prominent quality caveat, or whether the catalog should expose Gaia and HST values as co-equal alternatives. Do not average them.

issues.competing_evidence: Coppejans+16 §4.2 states the shortest significant variation is 69 min and reports 27.0±7.7 μJy followed by <17.5 μJy. Table A1 lists two adjacent Obs.2 bins at MJD 57080.15979 and 57080.17264, each 1110 s, with 27.0±7.7 μJy then <23.7 μJy; their midpoint separation is 1110 s (18.5 min). Table 3 gives whole Obs.2 <16.8 μJy.
issues.why_it_matters: The variability timescale and limit affect radio duty-cycle and cross-population comparisons.
issues.needed_action: Retain both the paper’s 69-min prose claim and the exact table bins; verify from original visibility timestamps or author clarification before publishing a single variability timescale.

issues.competing_evidence: Long+06 says reddening is not directly measured, cites Verbunt+87 E(B−V)=0 with upper limit 0.03 from absent 2200 Å feature, and assumes negligible reddening from NH. Harrison & Johnson+04 assumes AV=0 for outburst photometry. Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot returns AG=0.4338 and E(BP−RP)=0.2376, but its single-star model is inappropriate for this unresolved variable CV. The inherited Gaia GSP-Phot distance (94.3003 pc, bounds 93.91–94.61 pc) and Teff=4481.9 K are also single-star model outputs and are excluded from component values; the prior M_G derived from that distance is retained only as a superseded legacy calculation.
issues.why_it_matters: Dereddening changes CMD interpretation; Gaia model extinction must not be substituted for a measured binary reddening.
issues.needed_action: Keep M_G explicitly uncorrected and decide whether to publish no intrinsic color/M_G until original reddening evidence and an appropriate binary treatment are reviewed. Do not interpret GSP-Phot distance or Teff as CV component measurements; keep them in explicit pipeline-output fields only.

issues.competing_evidence: Long & Gilliland+99 and Marsh+90 primary abstracts were checked but their complete original scanned articles were not accessible in this pass; exact orbital period is visible in Echevarria+07 and Coppejans+16, while Long & Gilliland masses/K1 are quoted by Naylor+05 and the abstract. Historical 1977/1980s radio upper limits are summarized in Coppejans+16 but their original reports were not individually read.
issues.why_it_matters: Detailed original timing, calibration, and historical radio-limit methods cannot be fully checked from abstracts/secondary quotations.
issues.needed_action: If those values are needed for release-level claims, obtain the original scanned Long & Gilliland and Marsh papers and the historical radio reports; otherwise keep the stated access limitations in the public provenance record.

issues.competing_evidence: Ridder+23 Table 4 reports 1–10 and 0.1–10 keV fluxes from approximate 4XMM-DR11 conversions (full band minus soft bands for 1–10; full 0.2–12 used as approximate 0.1–10). Errors are raised to at least 10% and star-marked. A source-specific absorption convention/fit is not given, and radio observations are non-simultaneous.
issues.why_it_matters: X-ray/radio ratios depend on bandpass, spectral model, absorption convention, and state.
issues.needed_action: Keep these as approximate catalog-comparison fluxes; before luminosity/population comparison, choose a common X-ray band/model and retain an explicit absorption convention or return to native 4XMM products.

issues.competing_evidence: Coppejans+16 finds the sample more consistent with synchrotron than coherent emission from low polarization, but U Gem had insufficient S/N for a spectral index and no source-specific mechanism is established. Its 1977/1980s upper limits are secondary summaries only; original reports were not retrieved.
issues.why_it_matters: Mechanism labels can prematurely connect non-magnetic CV radio emission to a specific jet or evolutionary pathway; old limits have weaker provenance.
issues.needed_action: Retain mechanism as an interpretation, not a measurement; inspect original older radio references only if those historical limits are used quantitatively.
